findings.title: Subtract allowed lateness from each tenant watermark
findings.comment: The documented rule is to reject timestamps further behind the tenant watermark than allowed_lateness. Thus watermark 100 and allowance 30 yields cutoff 70, with timestamp 70 accepted because the comparison is strict <; windows.py:70 instead computes 130 and rejects both 70 and newer timestamp 110.

findings.title: Clear accumulated windows when flushing each batch
findings.comment: aggregate.py:85-87 promises to emit and retire but only snapshots. Because pipeline.py:50 reuses the same aggregator across paths, already-emitted windows remain open, are emitted again, absorb later readings into prior-batch totals, and accumulate for the full backfill.

findings.title: Load tenant configuration once per run
findings.comment: summarize_files calls load_tenant_limits inside the reading loop, and that function opens and parses tenants.json each time. Besides O(readings) I/O, this means readings within one invocation can use different limits if the file changes mid-run instead of one consistent configuration snapshot.

findings.title: Validate tenant configuration before lookup
findings.comment: tenants.py:41-48 assumes both the root and selected entry are mappings and converts max_value without type or finiteness validation. Direct checks show a list root and null default raise incidental AttributeError, while max_value NaN becomes float nan; pipeline.py:41 then evaluates every value > nan as false, silently disabling clipping.

coverage.lens: Scrutinize the per-tenant watermark cutoff arithmetic and boundary behavior for allowed lateness.
Trace the aggregator flush contract across batches, especially window retirement, duplicate output, and retained memory.
Examine per-reading tenant configuration loading for repeated I/O, malformed configuration handling, and consistent fallback behavior.
